Subject: Finova demo follow-up - perf targets, routing, and next steps

Hi Sara / Mike -

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Good to hear the team liked the latency and streaming behavior in the sandbox. Per promised follow-up, here's a concise recap of the performance discussion and the items we agreed to validate: 

1) Target SLOs (what Finova asked for):
   - P95 end-to-end response latency (for typical user prompts, ~150 tokens): US < 300ms, EU < 400ms, APAC < 600ms
   - Sustained throughput: 50 req/s per region (peak burst to 200 req/s)
   - Concurrency: average 8 concurrent requests per shard, up to 64 concurrent across the fleet during peak windows
   - Streaming: token-by-token streaming (SSE/websocket) for UX-sensitive flows with max initial token latency < 150ms

2) Data residency / routing needs:
   - EU customer traffic and logs must remain in EU regions; no cross-border logging to US control plane storage.
   - APAC region will be handled via our Singapore POP; require confirmation on encryption-at-rest keys and KMS placement.

3) Fallback / graceful degradation:
   - When regional capacity constrained, route to nearest region with model-variant downgrade (quantized model) with pre-agreed latency/quality tradeoffs.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Share SLO worksheet with estimated fleet configuration + cost (attached).
- Aditya to validate streaming end-to-end numbers on your representative prompt set.
- Connor to confirm KMS/region support and provide the network diagram for your security team.

Can you confirm the p95 targets above are the right bar to validate against, and share a small sample of representative prompts (100-200) so Aditya can run a paced load?

Marissa

marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

Hi Marissa -

Thanks - this summary is perfect and aligns with what we sketched during the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

- P95 numbers look reasonable. For EU data residency we need access logs and audit logs to remain in EU (Germany or Ireland). Is it possible to keep the audit/logging bucket inside our tenant-managed GCP project?
- For streaming: we need initial token latency < 150ms and sustained token pacing of ~20-30 tokens/sec for long responses (300-800 tokens).
- Throughput: the 50 req/s per region is our baseline; during Black Friday style peak, we could see bursts up to 350 req/s for short periods. Can Redwood autoscale fast enough (under 60s) or do we need warm reserved capacity?

We can share a sample of 150 prompts by EOB tomorrow. Procurement (cc'ed) will need the cost estimate + terms to start fast-track review.

Hi Sara -

Thanks for the fast reply. I ran an initial micro-benchmark against a similar model and prompt distribution; sharing high-level takeaways below (will follow up with raw logs once we run Finova's exact prompts):

- Measured p95 end-to-end (512-token cap, quantized v1 model): US-west (Oakland) ~ 260ms, EU (Frankfurt) ~ 360ms, APAC (Singapore) ~ 540ms under steady 50 req/s load.
- Streaming: initial token latency (time-to-first-byte) ~ 80-120ms; sustained token pace ~25 tokens/sec depending on model complexity and seq length.
- Concurrency & autoscaling: with Dedicated pools configured, we can achieve sub-60s scale-up for modest bursts (up to ~150% capacity) but for bursts >200% we recommend short warm capacity (reserved burst) to avoid cold-start tail.
- Routing: We can configure a regional routing policy (geo-IP + customer-override) and pin EU traffic to EU-only model hosts and EU KMS. For audit logs, we support an option to ship logs to a customer-managed GCS/S3 bucket placed in your region (we'll provide a signed connector).

I'll schedule a short run with your 150 prompts once Sara shares them; that will give us exact p95 numbers and token pacing per prompt.

Cheers,
Aditya

Wanted to add the network/security notes for your infra team: 

- KMS: We support customer-managed keys in all target regions (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). For EU-residency you can provision keys in the EU project and we'll configure host-side access via workload identity.
- Logging: We can deliver audit logs to your customer-managed storage (S3/GCS) and optionally mirror a subset to Redwood control plane for operational dashboards (only if you opt-in).
- Network: Recommended setup is a private peering/VPC-SC for Dedicated; for Hosted we support VPC egress via NAT and IP allowlists. Diagram attached.
